append.text: Ps 29:2 *quóniam suscepísti me* → *porque me amparastes* (the Matins antiphon and the versicle of 12-08 and of Our Lady Aparecida sing this colon, grep); passed the Latinist twice, heard rightly.

**Ps 29:2 *nec delectásti inimícos meos super me* → *e não alegrastes os meus inimigos à minha custa*:** delectáre causative is εὐφραίνω, this row's Greek verb, so by D15's test it shares *alegrar* (*deleitar* is bookish, and sensual). *super me* → *à minha custa* (the gloating relation; MS1932's words; *sobre mim* the option). Passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'at my expense'.

**Ps 29:4 *eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam* → *tirastes do inferno a minha alma*** — *tirar de* for the source, as this row foresees (MS1932 *tiraste*); *fizestes sair* the option. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 29:4 *eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam* → *tirastes do inferno a minha alma*:** kept (DRB *hell*; MS1932 *inferno* with a note, 'the grave'). The blind reader heard 'the place of eternal damnation' first, the world of the dead second — the fourth place so heard (after 6:6, 17:6, 15:10); here, as in 15:10, it is a soul brought back from it, where the damned's hell is the wrong sense. Passed the Latinist twice. *mundo dos mortos* is the option in Ps 29.

Ps 29:4 *salvásti me a descendéntibus in lacum* → *salvastes-me dos que descem à cova* (the row's formula); the blind reader heard 'saved me from dying' first, 'from those people' second — the Latin's own range.

**Ps 29 has it three times:** 29:5 *confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis ejus* → *dai graças à memória da sua santidade* (the blind reader found the dative to a 'memory' a little odd, and understood it), 29:10b *Numquid confitébitur tibi pulvis* → *Acaso o pó vos dará graças* (6:6's question again), 29:13 *in ætérnum confitébor tibi* → *para sempre vos darei graças*. D5 held; no reader objected.

**Ps 29:6b *Ad vésperum demorábitur fletus* → *À tarde se demorará o pranto: * e pela manhã, a alegria*** — the row's second place; the blind reader heard 'weeping will stay through the evening' first (right), 'will be slow to come' second. The stylist wanted the subject first (*O pranto se demorará à tarde*): refused, the two adverbs heading the cola are the Latin's antithesis; option in Ps 29.

append.row: | *Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum*
append.text: **Ps 29:7 *Non movébor in ætérnum* → *Para sempre não serei abalado*** — 14:5b's build, D23. **The second stylist to refuse it** («“para sempre não” soa transposta e faz hesitar sobre o alcance da negação» → *Jamais serei abalado*); the blind reader heard the scope rightly. Kept for the row; *Jamais* is option 2 in Ps 29. Wants the ruling this row already asks for.

Ps 29:8 *præstitísti decóri meo virtútem* → *destes vigor ao meu esplendor* (τῷ κάλλει μου; DRB *beauty*, MS1932 *prosperidade*): the row's word; the blind reader heard 'strengthened my greatness or my radiance'. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 29:8 *præstitísti decóri meo virtútem* → *destes vigor ao meu esplendor*** — the proposal *vigor* for a man's strength applied (given by God to the man's decor, not God's own power); passed the Latinist twice; *poder* the option.

**Ps 29:12 *Convertísti planctum meum in gáudium mihi … et circumdedísti me lætítia* → *Convertestes o meu lamento em júbilo para mim … e me cercastes de alegria*** — the row followed; gáudium and lætítia in one verse (the Greek χορόν / εὐφροσύνην), so *alegria* cannot serve both. The Ps 29 blind reader did not list *júbilo* as unknown (the Ps 20 reader did); the Latinist passed it twice; no stylist remark. Evidence for the ruling: *júbilo* holds here; *regozijo* is the option in Ps 29.

**Ps 29:10 *dum descéndo in corruptiónem* → *enquanto desço à corrupção*:** kept (the row; 15:10 = Acts 2:27). **The blind reader heard moral corruption as the likely hearing** («esse é o sentido mais corrente de “corrupção”»), decay second — the second place so heard. *decomposição* added as the option in Ps 29; for the row: the Acts places (15:10) have their own reason, 29:10 does not.
Ps 29:3 *clamávi ad te, et sanásti me* → *clamei a vós, * e me curastes* — the row's verb; the stylist's best line; the blind reader heard bodily healing first, inner second.

**Ps 29:11 *Dóminus factus est adjútor meus* → *o Senhor se fez o meu auxílio* — HELD against two Latinist MAJORS (drafts 1 and 2) asking *auxiliador*,** as 9:10 (*se fez refúgio … auxílio*), 17:19's build (*se fez o meu protetor*). No reader misheard it. Another place for the ruling this row asks.

**Ps 29:13 *et non compúngar* → *e eu não seja compungido*** (draft 2): draft 1's reflexive *não me compunja* (4:5's form) drew the Latinist's minor (the voice), the stylist's worst line («exige decifração») and the blind reader's unknown word; the passive participle keeps the Latin's voice and is current (*coração compungido*). The stylist's *não seja ferido* (the image, plainer) is the option. So the row now has the reflexive for the imperative (4:5 *compungi-vos*) and the passive for the passive.

**Ps 29:12 *Convertísti planctum meum in gáudium* → *Convertestes o meu lamento em júbilo*:** with *in* + result the verb is 'turn X into Y', which Portuguese says only with *converter em* (*voltar em* is not said), and no reader heard conversion. **Proposal:** *converter em* for change-into (65:6, 77:44, 104:29, 113:8 — grep). *Mudastes* the option.
Ps 29:6b *demorábitur fletus* → *o pranto*; kept apart from 29:12 *planctus* → *lamento* (κοπετός, the beating of the breast; see its row).

Ps 29:6 *et vita in voluntáte ejus* → *e vida na sua vontade*; 29:8 *in voluntáte tua* (instrumental) → *pela vossa vontade* — the noun repeats, the preposition follows the sense. Heard rightly both times.

**Ps 29:5 *Psállite Dómino, sancti ejus* → *Entoai salmos ao Senhor, vós, seus santos*:** the same danger (bare, *ao Senhor, seus santos* is heard as a second dative); with a possessive, *vós,* marks it better than *ó* (*ó seus santos* is the option). The row's rule then: mark the vocative — *ó* before a bare noun, *vós,* before a possessive. Passed the Latinist twice; heard rightly.

terms: | super me (joy / gloating over someone) | à minha custa (*e não alegrastes os meus inimigos à minha custa*) | open | Ps 29:2 (ἐπ᾽ ἐμέ). *sobre mim* after *alegrar* is heard as 'about me'; MS1932's idiom. Recurs in the family *ne supergáudeant mihi* (34:19, 34:24, 37:17 — grep before use). Passed the Latinist twice. |

| memória (of God, *memóriæ sanctitátis ejus*) | memória (*dai graças à memória da sua santidade*) | open | Ps 29:5; 96:12 *confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus* (another noun, grep). μνήμη. MS1932 *celebrai a sua santa memória*. The blind reader understood it. |
| indignátio | indignação (*há ira na sua indignação*) | working | Ps 29:6 (θυμῷ); kept apart from ira → ira and furor → furor. |

| abundántia | abundância (*na minha abundância*) | open | Ps 29:7 (εὐθηνία, 'prosperity'); 8 lines (grep: 32:17, 71:7, 77:25, 121:6, 121:7, 122:4, 144:7). The blind reader heard material goods first, well-being second — the Latin's range. MS1932 *prosperidade* the option. |
| præstáre | dar (*destes vigor ao meu esplendor*) | open | Ps 29:8 (παρέσχου); 18:8 *sapiéntiam præstans* (grep). *conceder* the option. |
| utílitas | proveito (*Que proveito há no meu sangue*) | open | Ps 29:10 only (grep; ὠφέλεια). MS1932 *utilidade* is heavy. |

| planctus | lamento (*Convertestes o meu lamento em júbilo*) | open | Ps 29:12 only (grep; κοπετός, the beating of the breast). Kept apart from fletus → pranto (29:6b, same psalm); MS1932 *pranto* merges them. DRB *mourning* → *luto* the option. |

| saccus | pano de saco (*rasgastes o meu pano de saco*) | open | Ps 29:12 only (grep; σάκκον). *o meu saco* is a bag in Portuguese and a vulgarity in Brazil; *pano de saco* keeps the word and says cloth, without explaining the mourning (MS1932's parenthesis *(de penitência)*). The blind reader listed it as unknown but heard 'a coarse cloth I wore'. cilícium (34:13, 68:12) is another word → *cilício*. |

| glória mea (the self) | a minha glória (*Para que a minha glória vos cante*) | open | Ps 29:13; 56:9 = 107:3 *Exsúrge, glória mea*, 107:2 *in glória mea* (grep; 3:4, 61:8 are of God). Not explained (MS1932 *a minha alma*). The blind reader heard honour personified, or the self. |

| clamábo … deprecábor (two futures ending both cola) | *hei de clamar … suplicarei* | open | Ps 29:9: *clamarei / suplicarei* rhymed at mediant and final (the stylist); the periphrastic future is the same tense. |
